items.title: IARPA Multi-View Stereo benchmark, full-size WorldView-3 PAN NITF (10 views over San Fernando, Buenos Aires) with DigitalGlobe metadata tars and JHU/APL lidar DSM truth for the challenge AOIs
items.source: IARPA / JHU-APL MVS benchmark (SpaceNet AWS bucket)
items.licence: IARPA Multi-View Stereo 3D Mapping benchmark (JHU/APL), hosted in the SpaceNet AWS bucket. Bucket license.txt: MIT-style permission notice, "Copyright 2016 The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory"; readme.txt: "Approved for Public Release; Distribution is Unlimited". Required citation: "A Multiple View Stereo Benchmark for Satellite Imagery", IEEE AIPR Workshop, October 2016. Commercial satellite imagery courtesy of DigitalGlobe (now Maxar/Vantor); the NITF headers carry DigitalGlobe licensing text, so redistribution relies on the public-release statement (same open question as rs-nitf-wv3-mvs-stereo-chips)
items.attribution: IARPA MVS benchmark (JHU/APL); commercial satellite imagery courtesy of DigitalGlobe. Cite: "A Multiple View Stereo Benchmark for Satellite Imagery", IEEE AIPR 2016
items.format: NITF2.1 (IC=C8 JPEG 2000, 11-bit, RPC00B, USE00A, 2 image segments incl. cloud mask) + DG tar (IMD/RPB/TIL/XML/ATT/EPH) + GeoTIFF lidar DSM
items.notes: Bucket listed in full (2,830 keys): WV3/PAN (50 NTF), WV3/MSI (50), WV3/SWIR (1), Lidar/LAZ (40 tiles, ~43 MB each), Challenge_Data_and_Software (Lidar_gt DSMs, kml polygons, crop software). Geometry from the IMD inside each tar. The 18DEC15 sweep gives 6 views in one pass with azimuth spread ~100 deg (convergence up to ~35 deg); 19DEC15 adds an opposite-azimuth view one day later; the 07JAN16 triplet is a narrow along-track set at high obliquity. Full images held as chips in rs-nitf-wv3-mvs-stereo-chips come from 140455 and 140554. NITF header parsed via Range: NUMI 2 (36864x43008 PAN, C8, blocks 42x36; 66x80 cloud mask, NC), TREs CSCRNA, CSEXRA, CSPROA, PIAIMC, RPC00B, STDIDC, USE00A, J2KLRA, HISTOA, CSCCGA. Lidar_gt DSMs are the per-AOI truth used by the challenge metrics; the raw lidar LAZ (and SBET) are in Lidar/ if point truth is wanted. Tars hold the DigitalGlobe delivery (IMD, RPB, TIL, XML, ATT, EPH, GIS shapes): extract them.
